title: Protocol for casein kinase 1γ3 CSNK1G3 gene knockout and recombinant gene expression in cultured HeLa cells
protocol: Digest the pSELECT-CRISPR-Cas9 plasmid with Esp3I.
Run the digested plasmid on a 1% agarose gel and excise and purify the linear backbone fragment, which is approximately 7.7 kbp in length.
Mix complementary oligonucleotides to a final concentration of 22 μM each in buffer [100 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0), 100 mM NaCl, 10 mM EDTA].
Incubate the mixed oligonucleotides in a block heater or thermal cycler.
Mix the purified digested plasmid with 250 fmol of the annealed oligonucleotides in a ligation reaction.
Incubate the ligation reaction at 16°C for 30 min.
Transform 3 μL of the ligated reaction into E. coli using competent bacteria.
Store the rest of the ligated reaction at -20°C as backup.
Plate the transformation mix onto LB broth agar plates containing 100 μg/mL of puromycin and incubate at 37°C for 16–18 hours.
Pick at least 10 colonies and re-streak on an LB-agar plate containing 100 μg/mL of puromycin and incubate at 37°C for 16–18 hours.
Inoculate 3–4 grown colonies individually in 3–5 mL of LB medium containing 100 μg/mL of puromycin and incubate at 37°C with vigorous shaking (e.g., 200–250 rpm) for 16–18 hours.
Harvest the bacterial cells and extract plasmids.
Verify the inserted sequence by Sanger sequencing and identify the positive clones.
Culture HeLa cells in D-MEM with 10% (v/v) FBS at 37°C, 5% CO2, and 100% humidity.
Seed HeLa cells on a 12-well plate (1.5 × 10^5 cells/well).
Culture the seeded cells for 18–24 h at 37°C.
Refresh the culture medium 30–60 min prior to transfection.
Prepare transfection mix as indicated and incubate at 20°C-25°C for 20 min.
Add the transfection mix dropwise to cells.
Culture the transfected cells at 37°C for 24 h.
Trypsinize cell monolayers with 200–300 μL of trypsin-EDTA.
Pour the cell suspension onto a 60-mm dish containing 5 mL of culture medium.
Add puromycin to a final concentration of 5 μg/mL.
Culture for 2–3 days at 37°C until non-transfected HeLa cells have died off completely.
Trypsinize the cell monolayers after culturing.
Transfer harvested cells onto a 12-well plate.
Culture puromycin-selected cells for 3–4 days to amplify them.
Count puromycin-selected cells from step 2.
Seed 100–200 cells in a 100-mm dish.
Spin down the remaining cells and resuspend them in CELLBANKER1.
Store the cell suspension at −80°C as bulk stock.
Confirm under a microscope that single cells have adhered to the dish.
Draw circles around at least 10 single cells using a permanent marker pen on the bottom of the dish.
Mark wells containing single cells on a 96 well plate.
Culture marked cells until colonies form, consisting of more than 10 cells (takes approximately 10–14 days).
Isolate the colonies and seed them onto both a 12-well plate and a 24-well plate.
Apply autoclaved grease to a cloning ring and place it on the dish over one colony.
Wash the cells inside the cloning ring with PBS (100 μL) and add trypsin-EDTA solution (50 μL).
Repeat washing procedure for other colonies.
Check under microscope that cells are detached from dish; add fresh medium to each cloning ring (200 μL).
Harvest cells by pipetting up and down, transferring suspensions into 1.5-mL tubes, and spinning down the cells.
Discard medium and resuspend cells in 1 mL of fresh medium.
Seed cell suspension on a 12-well plate (400 μL) and a 24-well plate (600 μL).
Add an additional 600 μL of fresh medium to the 12-well plate for total culture volume of 1 mL per well.
Culture cells until sub-confluence.
Use cells for verification of genome editing.
Prepare cell stocks of each clone using CELLBANKER1.
Trypsinize the cell monolayers and harvest them from the 24-well plate in 1.5-mL tubes.
Wash the cells twice with 500 μl of PBS.
Resuspend the washed cells in 100 μl of TE buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0; 1 mM EDTA).
Incubate the resuspended cells at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge the samples at 16,873 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant (DNA solution) to new 1.5-mL tubes.
Prepare the PCR reaction mix with the indicated components and primers from the key resources table.
Run 5 μl of the PCR reaction on a 2% agarose gel to verify amplification of the target region.
Verify the nucleotide lengths of PCR products corresponding to exon 5 and exon 12 as 500 bp and 457 bp, respectively.
Purify the remaining PCR reaction using QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (QIAGEN).
Elute the PCR product using 50 μL of H2O.
Use 5 μL of the eluted PCR product and primers for Sanger sequencing.
Perform a sequencing analysis of each locus after cloning the PCR product.
Eliminate any clonal effects by using independently isolated multiple clones for initial phenotype analysis.
Measure sensitivity to lysenin to identify successful C-terminal cleavage genome editing of the CSNK1G3 locus.
Seed cells from step 3 on a 12-well plate at a density of 2.5 × 10^4 cells per well.
Prepare three wells for each genome-edited cell line or the parental HeLa cells.
Culture the plates at 37°C for 18-24 hours.
Wash the cells once with 1 mL of serum-free medium.
Add 500 μL of serum-free medium supplemented with lysenin (final concentration 100 ng/mL) to three wells, and without lysenin to the other three wells.
Culture at 37°C for 2 hours.
Discard the medium from each well.
Add 250 μL of fresh serum-free medium to each well.
Add 250 μL of MTT solution (5 mg/mL thiazolyl blue tetrazolium bromide in PBS) to each well and mix by swirling the plate.
Incubate at 37°C for 3 hours.
Add 750 μL of MTT solvent (4 mM HCl in isopropanol) to each well and mix by swirling the plate.
Cover the plate with tin foil to protect from light.
Incubate at 20-25°C for 30 minutes with shaking on an orbital shaker.
Measure the absorbance at OD = 595 nm.
Prepare the PCR reaction mix as indicated.
Run the PCR reaction on a 1% agarose gel.
Purify the amplified HA-CK1G1 coding gene region from the gel, which is 1333 bp in length.
Elute the purified PCR product using 40 μL of H2O.
Digest 20 μL of the purified PCR product (HA-CK1G1 coding gene) with EcoRI and NotI restriction enzymes.
Digest 0.5 μg of pMXs-IRES-Neo vector with EcoRI and NotI restriction enzymes.
Precipitate the digested DNA using ethanol precipitation.
Dissolve the precipitated DNA in 5 μL of TE buffer (10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA).
Run 1 μL of DNA on a 1% agarose gel to estimate the amount in comparison with size marker bands.
Mix digested gene products and pMXs-IRES-Neo vector in an approximately 2:1 molar ratio.
Prepare a ligation reaction mix.
Incubate the ligation reaction at 16°C for 4–5 hours.
Transform 3 μL of the ligation reaction into E. coli using competent bacteria; store the rest at −20°C as backup.
Plate the transformation mix onto LB agar plates containing 100 μg/mL of ampicillin and incubate at 37°C for 16–18 hours.
Pick at least 10 colonies and subject them to colony PCR to identify positive clones with CSNK1G gene inserts.
Prepare a PCR reaction mixture and aliquot 15 μL into PCR reaction tubes.
Pick bacteria from each colony using a disposable tip and suspend them in the PCR reaction mixture.
Load 5 μL of PCR reaction on a 1% agarose gel and detect positive clones with PCR products of approximately 1.4 kbp.
Inoculate 3–4 positive colonies individually in 3–5 mL of LB medium containing 100 μg/mL of ampicillin and incubate at 37°C for 16–18 hours with vigorous shaking.
Harvest bacterial cells and extract plasmids.
Verify the inserted sequence by Sanger sequencing.
Identify positive clones (HA-CK1G1/pMXs-IRES-IN).
Sub-clone the CSNK1G2 gene region including the 5′UTR region into pcDNA3.1(+) vector.
Insert an HA-tag CDS between the 5′UTR and the CSNK1G2 CDS by PCR.
Transfer the 5′UTR-HA-CK1G2 DNA region into a retrovirus-based pMXs-IRES-Neo vector.
Run the PCR reaction on a 0.8% agarose gel.
Purify the amplified CSNK1G2 gene product using 40 μL of TE buffer.
Digest 5 μL of purified PCR product and pcDNA3.1(+) vector with EcoRI and XhoI restriction enzymes.
Dissolve digested DNA in TE buffer.
Mix the digested gene product against the pcDNA3.1(+) vector to prepare a ligation reaction mix.
Incubate the ligation reaction at 16°C for 16-18 hours.
Transform the ligated reaction into E. coli using competent bacteria.
Plate the transformation mix onto LB agar plates containing ampicillin.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 16-18 hours.
Inoculate 3–4 colonies individually in 3–5 mL of LB medium containing ampicillin and incubate at 37°C with vigorous shaking.
Harvest bacterial cells and extract plasmids.
Verify the inserted sequence by Sanger sequencing to identify positive clones (pcDNA/5′UTR-hCKIγ2).
Insert an HA-tag sequence in-frame with the CSNK1G2 CDS by PCR using primers from the key resources table.
Digest the PCR reaction with DpnI restriction enzyme and transform into E. coli.
Follow steps g–i to construct pcDNA/5′UTR-HA-hCKIγ2.
Digest 0.5 μg of pcDNA/5′UTR-HA-hCKIγ2 plasmid and pMXs-IRES-Neo vector with EcoRI and XhoI restriction enzymes.
Follow steps d–i to construct the HA-CK1G2/pMXs-IRES-IN plasmid.
Prepare total RNA from HeLa cells using a PureLink RNA Mini Kit.
Elute total RNA in 30 μL of RNase-free H2O.
Synthesize cDNA from 0.5 μg of total RNA and ReverTra Ace qPCR RT Master Mix.
Amplify the CSNK1G3 gene region by PCR using cDNA solution and a pair of primers.
Run the PCR reaction on a 1% agarose gel.
Purify the amplified CSNK1G3 gene product, which is 1277 bp in length.
Elute the PCR product using 40 μL of H2O.
Digest 10 μL of purified PCR product and 0.5 μg of pBSnHAcFL vector with SalI and KpnI restriction enzymes.
Reconstitute digested DNA in 5 μL of TE buffer.
Run 1 μL of DNA on a 0.8% agarose gel for estimation.
Mix the digested gene products and pBSnHAcFL vector in a 2:1 molar ratio.
Prepare the ligation reaction mix.
Incubate the ligation reaction at 16°C for 4-5 hours.
Transform 3 μL of the ligated reaction into E. coli using competent bacteria.
Store the rest of the ligated reaction at -20°C as backup.
Plate the transformation mix onto LB agar plates containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 16-18 hours.
Pick at least 10 colonies and subject them to colony PCR.
Prepare a PCR reaction mixture and aliquot 15 μL into PCR reaction tubes.
Suspend bacteria from each colony in the PCR reaction mixture.
Load 5 μL of PCR reaction on a 0.8% agarose gel for detection.
Detect positive clones with PCR products approximately 1.5 kbp.
Inoculate 3-4 positive colonies individually in 3-5 mL LB medium containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate at 37°C for 16-18 hours with vigorous shaking.
Harvest bacterial cells and extract plasmids.
Verify the inserted sequence by Sanger sequencing.
Digest 0.5 μg of HA-CK1G3/pBSnHAcFL plasmid and pMXs-IRES-Neo vector with EcoRI and NotI restriction enzymes.
Mix 100 μL of Opti-MEM with 3 μL of FuGENE6 Transfection Reagent (Promega) and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Add 1 μg of HA-CK1G/pMXs-IRES-IN plasmid to the mixture and incubate at 20°C–25°C for 20 minutes.
Add the mixture dropwise to Plat-E Retroviral Packaging cells cultured on a 6-well plate (8 × 10^5 cells/well) and culture at 37°C for 24 hours.
Refresh the medium after 24 hours and continue culturing at 37°C for an additional 18–24 hours.
Collect media using a 5-mL syringe and pass through a 0.45 μM filter to create virus stock.
Aliquot the virus stock into two tubes and store at −80°C.
Seed HeLa cells on a 6-well plate (1 × 10^5 cells/well) and culture at 37°C for 18–24 hours.
Discard media from cells and add the virus solution.
Prepare one well without the virus solution as a negative control for marker selection.
Incubate the cells at 37°C for 4 h.
Refresh the medium and culture the cells at 37°C for 18–24 h.
Trypsinize the cell monolayers, resuspend in medium supplemented with 400 μg/mL of G418, and transfer to a 60 mm dish.
Culture the cells at 37°C for 2–3 days, refreshing the medium (supplemented with G418).
When cells are sub-confluent, trypsinize monolayers again, resuspend in fresh culture medium, dilute cell suspension 3- to 4-fold with G418-supplemented medium, and transfer to a new 60 mm dish.
Repeat the dilution step until cells in the control well (without gene transfer) have died off completely.
Prepare cell stocks using CELLBANKER1 and store at -80°C.
Trypsinize the cell monolayers from a 6-well plate.
Wash twice with 500 μL of PBS.
Resuspend in 100 μL of TBS buffer containing 1% (v/v) Triton X-100 and cOmplete Protease Inhibitor Cocktail EDTA-free.
Incubate on ice for 10 min to lyse the cells.
Centrifuge the tubes at 16,873 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube.
Quantify the protein amount in the samples using the Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit.
Mix 25–50 μg of total protein sample with 12.5 μL of 4× NuPAGE LDS Sample Buffer supplemented with 100 mM dithiothreitol and up to 50 μL H2O.
Incubate the sample at 70°C for 5 min to denature the proteins.
Quickly chill on ice after heating.
Load 5-10 μg of total protein sample on a 7.5% SDS-polyacrylamide gel.
Run the gel at a constant current of 20-30 mA per gel for 60-90 min depending on the gel size.
Transfer proteins to a PVDF membrane immersed in transfer buffer using Mini Trans-Blot Cell at a constant voltage of 30 V for 16-17 h at 4°C or at 100 V for 1 hour.
Block the PVDF membrane with TBS-T containing 5% skimmed milk for 30 min at 20-25°C.
Rinse the PVDF membrane with TBS-T and incubate with anti-HA-HRP conjugate antibody diluted 5000-fold in TBS-T containing 1% skimmed milk for 1 h at 20-25°C.
Wash the PVDF membrane for 5 min at 20-25°C with TBS-T, repeating this step two more times.
Visualize HA-CK1G signals using Immobilon Western Chemiluminescent HRP Substrate.
